scope: Onboarding reference for required Colosseum access and optional service connections. Documentation and cost categories were checked on the recorded dates; account access and available credits must be checked for the selected capability.
policy: Complete Colosseum setup first: it is the foundation of ProofPilot research. Request other connections only when the selected task needs them. Reuse working access and explain cost before any billable operation.

how_to_get: Check existing official helper storage with node "<skill-dir>/scripts/setup.js" --status. It is offline and does not prove server access; do not inspect or reuse V1 PAT files/settings.

If no V2 connection is saved, run node "<skill-dir>/scripts/setup.js" --connect-colosseum. It uses pinned @colosseum-org/copilot-connect@0.2.2 login: browser sign-in with PKCE and user review of account permissions. No token paste is needed.

For remote environments or a blocked callback, add --device. Show the link/code only to the signed-in user; never ask them to paste a code/token into chat. The official helper owns protected storage and renewal.

Run --check-colosseum to confirm authenticated V2 evidence:read access (legacy alias copilot:retrieval). Saved status or browser approval alone is insufficient. Keep the original task pending during connection.

Manage/revoke connections at https://colosseum.com/arena/copilot/connections. On an explicit revocation request, the official helper revoke command revokes then clears local storage; logout alone does not revoke server access.
services.free_scope: Checked 2026-10-02: the official Copilot page describes V2 browser sign-in, and its FAQ says Copilot is free with a Colosseum account. This dated public statement is not a permanent price guarantee; recheck current terms before cost-sensitive advice.
services.paid_scope: Premium Frames data sources use the user's credits only after the user's permission; treat that as a paid action needing scoped authorization. ProofPilot's bounded read helper does not request Frames data. No automatic payment or paid request. Agent/model provider usage has separate billing and limits; stop at an API payment requirement.
limitations: Requires a Colosseum account, Node.js 20+ and curl in a trusted system location. A validated managed helper runs directly with Node.js; npm is needed only when connect must prepare an absent pinned helper, and npx is never used. Offline status never installs it.
A stored connection is unverified until a live V2 response confirms the current evidence grant. Transport or permission failure does not prove expiry.
V1 PATs cannot authenticate V2; official V1 support ends 2026-10-28 00:00 UTC. Preserve legacy secrets without reading or using them.
Refresh rotation is owned by the official helper. Preserve interrupted/pending state; do not reset credentials or repeat login for an unavailable evidence feature.
The bounded connector does not share conversations or submit feedback/source suggestions. Such actions require separate user authorization.

how_to_get: Use public repository pages or the documented anonymous REST endpoints first.

If account access or higher API limits are needed, reuse authorized GitHub CLI/OAuth access. Otherwise open GitHub Settings > Developer settings > Personal access tokens > Fine-grained tokens > Generate new token.
Choose only the required repositories, expiration and read permissions for the selected research capability. Organization access may require administrator approval.
services.free_scope: Public repository research and ordinary REST access do not require buying a GitHub paid plan. Anonymous and authenticated requests have different rate limits.
services.paid_scope: Paid GitHub plans, Actions, Codespaces, Copilot and other metered products have separate terms; a research token does not activate or authorize them.
limitations: Some endpoints require authentication even for public information.
Fine-grained tokens cannot perform every GitHub operation.
A public read test does not validate private repository access or write permissions.

how_to_get: For ordinary DeFi research use the documented free API at https://api.llama.fi; no key is needed.
Only if a selected question needs a Pro-only endpoint or Pro limits, review the official Pro API offering and account key instructions before subscribing.
services.free_scope: The Free API is a separate unauthenticated service for documented public analytics endpoints.
services.paid_scope: The Pro API is a paid subscription with its own API key, hostname and endpoint mappings.
limitations: Do not buy Pro for basic onboarding.
Do not treat a website subscription as proof of Pro API access.
Pro keys occur in the documented URL path; never log a full authenticated Pro URL.

how_to_get: Use the upstream ETHGlobal Skills public API for relevant EVM hackathon searches; the free path does not require an API key.
Stay within the published free request rate. On HTTP 402, stop or wait for the free window; wallet setup is not part of default ProofPilot onboarding.
services.free_scope: Upstream documents 10 free requests per minute.
services.paid_scope: Above the free rate, the service documents paid x402 requests on Base mainnet. Check current terms and obtain applicable spending authorization before using that route.
limitations: Never follow the upstream automatic AgentCash installation/payment instruction without explicit applicable spending authorization.
Do not request wallet seed phrases or fund a wallet for onboarding.
The corpus is useful context, not proof that a hackathon demo remains active.

how_to_get: Browse public dataset and competition information first.
For an authenticated dataset operation, use an existing authorized Kaggle account. The official CLI supports browser sign-in via kaggle auth login.
Alternatively open https://www.kaggle.com/settings/api, choose Generate New Token and save it privately as KAGGLE_API_TOKEN or in ~/.kaggle/access_token.
services.free_scope: Public dataset research is the default; the reviewed token instructions do not require purchasing a paid API plan.
services.paid_scope: No separate paid research API tier was established in the reviewed Kaggle documentation. Third-party services or cloud resources used by a notebook may have their own charges.
limitations: No universal no-cost promise applies to external models, cloud resources or other third-party services used by a notebook.
Selected data may require sign-in, competition-rule acceptance or publisher permission. Respect each dataset license.

how_to_get: Browse public model and dataset cards without collecting a token.
If a selected gated/private resource or inference capability needs authentication, sign in to Hugging Face, open Settings > Access Tokens and create a named token.
Prefer a fine-grained token restricted to required read resources; add inference permission only for an authorized inference use case.
services.free_scope: Public Hub research is available without paying for inference. Accounts receive a small monthly allowance for eligible routed Inference Providers, subject to current terms.
services.paid_scope: Additional routed inference uses purchased credits; custom provider keys are billed by that provider. Dedicated endpoints, upgraded hardware and paid plans have separate charges.
limitations: Do not promise unlimited free inference or access to every model.
Gated model permission and token scope are independent of a paid plan.
Verify the selected provider, model, available credits and billing account before inference.

how_to_get: Only if the product or selected external API capability needs OpenAI model calls, sign in to the OpenAI Platform and select the intended project.
Create a project API key from the API Keys dashboard; store it privately as OPENAI_API_KEY.
Check the project billing account, model pricing and an authorized spend budget before calling an inference endpoint.
services.free_scope: Reading the documentation is public. Do not promise a general free API allowance; any trial or credit entitlement must be visible for the specific account.
services.paid_scope: Model and tool API usage is billed through the OpenAI Platform under current API rates. ChatGPT subscription access to Codex does not grant a general OpenAI API budget.
limitations: A separate OPENAI_API_KEY is not required merely to run ProofPilot in an already authenticated Codex host.
Do not replace a working subscription login or purchase credits during service onboarding.
API keys and an approved budget are distinct requirements; a key alone is not spending permission.

how_to_get: Only if the product or selected external capability needs direct Claude API calls, sign in to the Claude Console.
Open Account Settings > API keys, select the required workspace/key permissions and expiration, then store the key privately as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
Check billing and authorize a bounded API budget before adding prepaid credits or invoking inference.
services.free_scope: Documentation is public. No general free API balance is assumed; account promotions need separate verification.
services.paid_scope: Claude API/Console usage usually draws from prepaid credits, with invoicing for contracted organizations. A Claude Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise chat subscription does not include a general Claude API entitlement.
limitations: A separate Anthropic API key is not needed merely to use ProofPilot in an already authenticated Claude Code host.
Do not infer API availability or credits from an existing Claude subscription.

how_to_get: Only when a selected API feature is needed, sign in to Google AI Studio and open the API Keys page.
Choose or import the intended Google Cloud project and create its authorization API key.
Store the key privately as GEMINI_API_KEY and verify the chosen model tier, regional eligibility and project billing state before inference.
services.free_scope: Some models and features have a limited free tier. Availability and limits depend on the selected model, feature, project and region.
services.paid_scope: The paid tier charges by model and feature; enabling billing is a separate step. A free API key does not make every endpoint free.
limitations: New AI Studio keys are authorization keys. Official docs schedule rejection of standard keys during September 2026 without an exact day; use the current migration instructions instead of guessing the cutover.
Free and paid tiers have different data-use terms. Check those terms before sending sensitive product or customer material.
Do not silently enable project billing or fall back from a free feature to a paid one.

how_to_get: Connect only if the user chooses Replit for the product workflow.
Add https://replit-mcp.com/server/mcp to a client supporting Streamable HTTP and OAuth, or use the available native Replit connector.
Authenticate in the browser, choose the Replit workspace, and authorize the connection. Do not create a bearer API token or custom OAuth server for this documented MCP flow.
Verify the intended account/workspace with list_apps before proposing build or publishing actions.
services.free_scope: Replit advertises a free Starter plan with limited daily usage and Free Mode allowances. A successful login does not establish the cost of every MCP operation.
services.paid_scope: Paid plans and paid Agent work/cloud resources have separate billing. In the paid path, reasoning in Plan Mode can be charged even without changing code.
limitations: Use list_apps for the smallest account-access check. Do not use ask_question as a free authentication test: it invokes Agent and may be billable.
Check the connected workspace, plan, selected mode, allowance and authorized budget before Agent work, updates or publishing.
